source.author: stat
source.text: Stat super occiduae nebulosa cubilia noctis Aethiopasque alios, nulli penetrabilis astro, lucus iners, subterque cavis grave rupibus antrum it vacuum in montem, qua desidis atria Somni securumque larem segnis Natura locavit, limen opaca Quies et pigra Oblivio servant et numquam vigili torpens Ignavia voltu.
source.text_original: Stat super occiduae nebulosa cubilia noctis / Aethiopasque alios, nulli penetrabilis astro, / lucus iners, subterque cavis grave rupibus antrum / it vacuum in montem, qua desidis atria Somni / securumque larem segnis Natura locavit, / limen opaca Quies et pigra Oblivio servant / et numquam vigili torpens Ignavia voltu.
source.text_english: There stands over the dim resting-places of the western night, and over the other Aethiopians, a sluggish grove, impenetrable to any star, and beneath it a cavern, heavy beneath hollow rocks, empty within a mountain, where lazy Nature has placed the halls of sluggish Somnus and his secure dwelling-place. The threshold is guarded by shadowed Quies and sluggish Oblivio, and torpid Ignavia, never wakeful in countenance.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: proximus hinc Butes Actaeis dives ab oris; innumeras nam claudit apes longaque superbus fuscat nube diem, dum plenas nectare cellas pandit et in dulcem reges dimittit Hymetton.
reuse.text_original: proximus hinc Butes Actaeis dives ab oris; / innumeras nam claudit apes longaque superbus / fuscat nube diem, dum plenas nectare cellas / pandit et in dulcem reges dimittit Hymetton.
reuse.text_english: Next from here was Butes, rich from the Actaean shores; for he keeps innumerable bees shut up and, proud, darkens the day with a long cloud, as he opens the cells full of nectar and sends the kings out into sweet Hymettus.
